newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil summons ambassadors to talk about trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil summons ambassadors to talk about trade.

text.p: Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso has summoned ambassadors from key international capitals to a meeting in Brasilia Wednesday to talk about trade, a spokeswoman said.
The spokeswoman for the Presidential Palace said the meeting, which comes amid concerns over Brazil's widening trade deficit, would take place over lunch.
Envoys to the European Union, the United States, the World Trade Organization, Argentina, Britain, Spain and the Organization of American States (OAS) will attend, she added.
Finance Minister Pedro Malan, Planning Minister Antonio Kandir, Foreign Minister Luiz Felipe Lampreia and Industry and Commerce Minister Francisco Dornelles will also be present.

The Ministry of Industry and Commerce said Tuesday the country posted an $819 million trade gap in the first three weeks of March, bringing the deficit for the year so far to $2.8 billion, more than half last year's $5.5 billion.
Officials say Brazil faces no problems in financing its current account gap, equivalent to 3.27 percent of gross domestic product last year.

They counter fears over the country's external accounts and an expected trade deficit this year in excess of $8.0 billion by noting foreign direct investment was expected to cover at least 40 percent of the current account gap in 1997.
The presidential spokeswoman said no detailed agenda had been prepared for the lunch but that the idea was to discuss Brazil's trade promotion campaigns.
The government has already taken some steps to boost exports -- making some exempt from tax, providing special credit lines and reviving an export insurance agency.
